headings.text: Why a hierarchy, not one big hub or a mesh
One pipeline, parameterized by the structure

blocks.html:
A hub-to-hub link is the unit of scale. Repeat it and you get a larger structure: one hub per group of servers, all federated to a central hub.

The pattern

For a large organization with several groups, each group running a few Deploy App TAK servers (say, five groups of three servers, 15 in total):

group 1: 3 servers ─▶ [Group 1 Hub] ─┐
  group 2: 3 servers ─▶ [Group 2 Hub] ─┤
  group 3: 3 servers ─▶ [Group 3 Hub] ─┼─▶ [Central Hub]
  group 4: 3 servers ─▶ [Group 4 Hub] ─┤
  group 5: 3 servers ─▶ [Group 5 Hub] ─┘

• Each group hub federates its own servers (single-hub guide), giving a full picture within the group, kept local.
  • Each group hub has one hub-to-hub link to the central hub (this guide), filtered to the shared SHARED_COP group.
  • The central hub brokers the common operating picture between groups; nothing else crosses.

Link count stays linear. With five groups of three: 15 server-to-hub links plus 5 group-to-central links is 20, versus 105 for a flat 15-server mesh. Adding a group is one more hub-to-hub link, not N more.

Why a hierarchy, not one big hub or a mesh

  • Localized traffic. Intra-group CoT never touches the inter-group links; only SHARED_COP crosses up. This matters on constrained bandwidth.
  • Graceful degradation. If the link to the central hub drops, each group keeps its own picture. A single shared hub would make hub loss an outage for everyone.
  • Releasability maps to the structure. The central hub's edges are the one place that governs cross-group sharing.

Enable MFDT (MongoDB) on the hubs so mission and Data-Sync changes store and forward across disrupted links and reconcile on reconnect.

One pipeline, parameterized by the structure

Because every link is derived from topology, the whole structure is one idempotent deployment parameterized by the group layout:

  • Inputs: the list of groups, their servers, and the shared group taxonomy (tak_SHARED_COP, plus any sub-pictures like tak_SHARED_FIRES).
  • Per group: stand up its servers plus a group hub (single-hub guide).
  • Per group hub: cross-trust with the central hub and add one filtered inter-hub edge (this guide).
  • Reconcile: adding or removing a group, or changing what is shared, is a re-render and re-apply, with no graphs drawn by hand.

Going further

The same hub-to-hub primitive composes further. A central hub can federate to another hub above it (multi-hop again), or two central hubs can link for a combined picture, with each boundary filtered to exactly the group that should cross. Keep every inter-hub edge narrow by default and widen it deliberately.
